title: Text Adventure Room
story: You are in a dark room. There's a door to the north and a chest in the corner. What do you do? Text adventures were the original video games — pure imagination powered by code. Build a single room with description, items, and choices that react to player input.
why: A text adventure combines enums for game state, structs for rooms/items, match for command processing, and if/else for game logic — a complete interactive experience.
analogy: A Choose-Your-Own-Adventure book where you flip to different pages based on your choices. Your text adventure is digital version: the 'page' is the current room description, 'choices' are parsed commands, and the 'story' branches based on player state (has key? chest open?).
try_it: Add more commands: 'inventory' (show player items), 'search' (find hidden items), 'use [item]' (combine items). Add a puzzle: need key from chest, torch to see, sword to fight monster. Track game state with an enum: Playing, Won, Lost.
tips: Use String matching on commands — simple, readable, easy to extend
Track game state with enums: Playing, Won, Lost, Quit
Each command should return feedback — the player needs to know what happened
common_mistakes: Not updating BOTH the room and player state on item pickups
Commands that work only once and never again — track state changes
Forgetting to handle unknown commands gracefully with 'You can't do that.'
